subject: BlueForge performance validation — coordination & new slot
messages:
From: Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@blueforge.io>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30 16:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick sync — perf validation prep

Diego / Laura —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. BlueForge engineering wants to move from a demo to a focused performance validation so we can validate expected throughput in our staging topology before committing to a Dedicated capacity pilot. Key asks from my side:
- A reproducible test run that targets our production-like workload (mixed chat + long-form generation).
- Clear pass/fail criteria (throughput targets, p95/p99 latency).
- A short window where we can observe KV cache behavior under sustained traffic.

Can we set a 2-hour deep-dive next week to walk through the test plan and schedule the load runs? We're in ET; ideal windows: 10:00–12:30 ET or 14:00–17:00 ET next Tue/Wed.

I've attached a simple topology sketch and sample request distribution for context.

Attachments: blueforge_topology.pdf (application/pdf)

—Sam
Sam Hayes
Principal SRE, BlueForge
sam.hayes@blueforge.io
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@blueforge.io>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31 09:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick sync — perf validation prep

Sam —

Thanks — this is exactly the right next step. We can absolutely run a reproducible validation with pass/fail gates. Preliminary targets we'd recommend based on the topology you sent:
- Target sustained throughput: 60k tokens/sec across the test cluster (aggregate).
- P95 latency target: < 180 ms for short chat flows; p99 < 350 ms.
- 30-minute ramp, 90-minute steady-state run, repeat x2.

Before we lock a calendar slot we have a few operational asks:
- Provide the CIDR blocks for allowlisting (we'll give our IPs from the hosting pool).
- Confirm whether requests will include tool-calls / function-calling (this impacts token footprint).
- Attach any representative prompt sets you want included in the run.

Proposed initial deep-dive slots (all ET):
- Tue 2026-09-01 10:30–12:30 ET
- Tue 2026-09-01 15:00–17:00 ET
- Wed 2026-09-02 11:00–13:00 ET

I'm looping in Marissa (customer success lead) and Soojin (performance SM) to confirm availability and compute profile recommendations. I'll follow up with a detailed test-plan and an allowlist we need you to open.

Attachments: perf-test-plan-v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick sync — perf validation prep

Team —

Confirming availability and runway: I can take Tue 10:30–12:30 ET but not the afternoon slot. Soojin — can you lead compute sizing? For BlueForge's profile (mixed chat + long-form), my baseline ask is: 8xA100-80GB (or equivalent with quantization profile q4f16) and network fixtures for 2x sustained clients. We'll propose a fallback with 4xA100 and higher batching if necessary.

Sooj, please add any tooling notes (load generator, traffic shape, secrets handling). I'll prepare the customer-facing readout template and add a HubSpot activity once slot is locked.

—Marissa

Date: 2026-09-02 15:43 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick sync — perf validation prep

Sam —

Thanks for the flexibility. BlueForge confirmed internal scheduling conflicts so we're moving to Wed 2026-09-02 11:00–13:00 ET (we'll keep the two-hour deep-dive + 90-minute run window). I've updated the calendar and attached the .ics.

Practical checklist before the session:
- BlueForge to open network allowlist for our test runner IPs (attachment: ip-allowlist.txt).
- We need a representative prompt set file (if you prefer, upload to the Google Doc below).
- Confirm whether function-calling will be exercised (yes/no).

Planned test run profile (high level):
- Ramps: 30-minute linear ramp to 60k tokens/sec aggregate.
- Steady state: 90 minutes at target throughput.
- Runs: 2 independent steady-state runs separated by a 20-minute cooldown.
- Metrics we will collect: per-route token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, KV hit ratio, GPU utilization, tail-latency traces.
- Pass criteria (example): sustained throughput within +/-5% for 90% of steady-state window AND p99 latency < 350 ms.

Links & artifacts:
- Test plan (editable): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcPerfPlan/edit
- HubSpot: HS-48291

Attachments: calendar-invite.ics (text/calendar), ip-allowlist.txt (text/plain)

If all good I'll send a final agenda and the shared drive folder with scripts and runner credentials (short-lived tokens) by EOD. Appreciate the quick coordination — see you Wed.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
